messages:
maria: Quick sync — I ran a micro-bench for compact-on-alloc + prewarm buffers when packing two small Llama variants on a single 80GB A100. Saw a spike in kernel-selection falling back to slower matmul path around step 420 which correlates with an OOM+swap event. attaching perf slice and config we used.

jon: Can you paste the exact allocator flags and batching config?

maria: sure — we used the experiment flags from last week: 
```
ALLOC_STRATEGY=compact_on_alloc
PREWARM_BUFFERS=1
KV_CACHE_POLICY=soft-priority
BATCH_WINDOW_MS=6
MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=4096
WORKSPACE_TARGET=0.8
```
We also set per-model soft quotas: model-A=28G, model-B=28G, reserve=24G for OS + ephemeral.

siva: interesting. compact_on_alloc can fragment if small free blocks accumulate, causing the runtime to fall back to the generic kernel that assumes contiguous workspace. Did you capture free list histograms?

maria: yes — here's a short excerpt from the profiler at t=418 (right before the fallback):
```
free_buckets: [64MB:2, 32MB:1, 16MB:0, 8MB:5, 4MB:12, 2MB:30]
alloc_requests: [kv: 600MB, activation: 900MB, temp: 120MB]
compaction_runs: 3 (last at t=412)
kv_hits: 0.81, kv_evictions: 12 (most from model-B)
kernel_selection: fast_gemm: 86%, generic_gemm: 14% -> after step 420 generic_gemm 49%
```

anya: 0.81 kv hit rate is decent but evictions look high. Are evicted KV blocks the same shape as allocations causing fragmentation when reallocated?

maria: yes, many evicted blocks were 64MB-ish kv pages for model-B. When model-A ramped, it allocated similar-sized activation buffers and compact_on_alloc couldn't coalesce quickly enough.

dmitri: two ideas: 1) add a small prefresh window where hot KV pages are compacted to a reserved slab before eviction; 2) tune prewarm to allocate a fixed pool of reusable temp buffers to avoid scatter. Both reduce churn.

jon: can you try a run with PREWARM_BUFFERS=4 and WORKSPACE_TARGET=0.72 and measure kernel selection? Also set KV_CACHE_POLICY=keep-hot to bias not evicting recently-used kv pages.

maria: kicking off now. will post results in ~5m.

deploy-bot: build 2026.3.17-rc7 deployed to canary GPUs (pools: canary-1). Notifying eng-runtime.

(5m later)

maria: quick results: PREWARM_BUFFERS=4 + keep-hot reduced generic_gemm fallback to 7% and eliminated the OOM-swap path entirely. kv_evictions dropped from 12->3. latency p95 improved ~8%. attaching the condensed perf log.

siva: nice. do we have a regression risk for extremely fragmented workloads where keep-hot might starve new models?

maria: good point — in a second run I added a soft-age threshold so keep-hot only protects pages younger than 30s; older cold pages become fair-evict. That preserved throughput and prevented starvation.

jon: can we codify this into a prioritized-evict policy: prefer small cold pages first, then largest fragments last, and allow compaction every N allocations (configurable). We should also expose the soft-age in the console as a tuning knob.

anya: also recommend an instrumentation change: emit a compactability_metric that reports contiguous-largest-free-chunk per GPU by model tag. That'll help routing and packing heuristics.

maria: agreed. I'll open a quick RFC with microbenchmark numbers attached. Draft snippet for config proposal: 
```
kv_evict_policy: prioritized
  - prefer: [small_cold, oldest]
  - protect_hot_seconds: 30
  - compaction_frequency: per_1e5_allocs
prewarm: { temp_pool: 4, pool_max_size_mb: 512 }
alloc: { strategy: compact_on_alloc, workspace_target: 0.72 }
batching: { window_ms: 6, max_batch_tokens: 4096 }
```

dmitri: we should run that config through the co-residency simulator with 3 models (one large, two small) and measure tail latency + cost per token. If sims look good, ship to canary.

jon: one more thing — add a trace tag when kernel selection falls back to generic_gemm so we can correlate with allocator state in logs. currently it's noisy to debug postmortems.

maria: yep adding trace tag now. I'll also attach a short flame chart showing the hotpath before/after change in the RFC. Anything else?

anya: can we add a test in perf-ci that simulates interleaved kv churn to catch regressions?

maria: on it. thanks all. :thumbsup:
